title: opencode-screencast
description: an OpenCode plugin for live herbstluftwm screencasts: floating narration and delegation windows, a geometry toolkit for the floating layer (disjoin_rects partitioning, batch fitting, tiling surgery), audience callbacks over dunst, and a typed OOP scenario layer whose runs serialize to replayable script files.

content.heading: opencode-screencast - the agent performs, the audience watches
content: **opencode-screencast** turns an **OpenCode** agent into a screencast performer: it spawns floating narration windows the audience reads while the agent drives **herbstluftwm** live - every hlwm operation logged into the narration feed, every delegated command typed visibly into managed terminals, completion signaled by sentinels instead of window-title guesses.

content.heading: the stage it performs on
content: three systems host the show: **herbstluftwm** (the floating layer is the stage floor - every narration and delegation window lives there), **dunst** (the audience's channel - whispers replace themselves in a stable slot or carry click actions), and **OpenCode** (the performer - a plugin host whose tool calls drive hlwm over herbstclient).
the floating layer is finite screen space shared with the user's own floats - occlusion is a layout bug, not cosmetics.

content.heading: the package, architecturally
content: an OpenCode plugin (hook-based tool integration) over a geometry toolkit and a typed scenario layer.

the geometry toolkit partitions the monitor with disjoin_rects against every decorated float: the largest unobscured rect becomes the placement slot, and a fit_floating_layer pass walks the whole floating layer into non-overlapping positions - nudging visibly by default, or snapping at once under the hlwm lock.
a single misplaced tile gets frame surgery instead: the split runs along the floating window's decorated edge so the covered tiled window lands on the free side.

the scenario layer authors presentations as typed OOP: branded winids and tag names, a Camera that carries the performance with it, managed Clients, and Scenes that record every action with millisecond offsets - saved as replayable .scenario.json files.

content.heading: usage - the scenario surface
content: the User surface reads like a test framework: expect, await, recover, awaitClick - predicates over hlwm observables (focus, floating state, rects, command exit codes, current tag) with recovery strategies instead of blind sleeps.
scenes record as they run; the saved .scenario.json replays the performance step for step.

a backprop-style checker walks each scene's action stream against simulated state and flags the churn that reads as screen flashes: duplicated camera moves, yo-yo focus, undone moves, float oscillation.

content.heading: quirks
content: the conversation window's winid churns when reopened - identity comes from capture-at-start, verified at every assert; the guarded close refuses to ever terminate it.
whisper click actions fire detached handlers through herbstclient - no blocked tooling.
the stranded roll-call audits the backstage windows (orchestrator, narration) for wrong tags, minimization, or drifting off-screen.

content.heading: stable so far - v0.1.x
content: sentinel-based completion (no window-title guesses), capture-at-start window identity, and the disjoin_rects placement slot are the stable floor of the plugin.
the scenario layer's recording format (.scenario.json) is the replayable surface.
